item.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Scale Workloads to Zero with HorizontalPodAutoscaler (4 minute read)
item.description: Kubernetes v1.37 makes horizontal pod autoscaling to zero replicas a Beta feature, enabled by default. A HorizontalPodAutoscaler can now scale a workload all the way down to zero pods and bring it back up based on object or external metrics, without requiring an add-on or Alpha feature gate as previous versions did. The feature works for queue consumers and batch processors but requires at least one object or external metric, since CPU and memory metrics disappear once no pods are running. The first Alpha version shipped in Kubernetes v1.16, and SIG Autoscaling plans to collect operational feedback before considering a GA graduation.

item.title: Security Incident - BGP Hijacking (12 minute read)
item.description: An unauthorized BGP announcement diverted traffic for a Softaculous-owned /24 for roughly 33 hours, allowing the attacker to intercept requests and obtain valid Let's Encrypt certificates because ACME validation traffic was hijacked too. A small number of Virtualizor systems later downloaded a malicious update package, showing how routing attacks can cascade into software supply-chain compromise.

item.title: Migrating a critical Kubernetes deployment from the default namespace without any downtime (6 minute read)
item.description: A Kubernetes engineer describes how to move a service out of the default namespace without downtime, using an ExternalName service as a DNS-level forwarding address. The approach lets dozens of dependent services keep calling the old cluster-internal DNS name while traffic silently routes to the new deployment, with no code changes required from other teams. A temporary policy exception handled the ingress side, allowing both the old and new ingress rules to coexist briefly while traffic was confirmed on the new deployment before the old one was removed.

item.title: Managed PostgreSQL vs. self-hosted PostgreSQL: Key benefits and trade-offs (6 minute read)
item.description: Managed PostgreSQL services reduce the operational tax of self-hosting by transferring infrastructure, patching, backups, high availability, and platform security responsibilities to the provider. Self-managed PostgreSQL remains preferable when organizations need deep control, specialized configurations, unsupported extensions, or have mature platform engineering and operational capabilities.

item.title: Metal3 meets KubeVirtBMC: Provisioning KubeVirt VMs like bare metal (6 minute read)
item.description: KubeVirtBMC can be paired with Metal3, a CNCF incubating project, to provision KubeVirt virtual machines as if they were physical bare-metal servers. Metal3 uses OpenStack Ironic under the hood to handle hardware inspection, boot device control, and OS image writing via standard IPMI or Redfish interfaces. KubeVirtBMC creates virtual BMC endpoints for KubeVirt VMs, so Metal3 has no way to distinguish them from real hardware. This post walks through a full end-to-end setup that configures Redfish virtual media boot without PXE or DHCP and provisions a VM with a live ISO image.

It profiles your machine, recommends models that fit your available memory, then downloads and runs them. The tool works with Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, Claude Code, Oh My Pi, and Cline, and also supports custom GGUF models from Hugging Face.

item.title: How we could save petabytes of cache storage with Zstandard and Pingora (7 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare has prototyped a system called Cache Transcoding that compresses eligible cached assets using the Zstandard algorithm before writing them to disk, shrinking those assets to roughly one-third of their original size on average. The system targets compressible text content like HTML, JSON, CSS, and JavaScript, which made up 67.3% of requests in Cloudflare's traffic sample but arrived uncompressed about 71% of the time. Encoding happens once when an asset enters the cache, while the CPU cost of decoding is paid on every serve at approximately 1.56 nanoseconds per byte. In testing across 10 cache servers with more than a million requests, the architecture stayed within its CPU budget at zstd level 3 with a 4 kibibyte minimum object size.

item.title: How Swiss Tables Work in Go's Built-in Map (28 minute read)
item.description: Go's newer map implementation uses a Swiss Table design that groups entries in small blocks with compact control bytes, allowing many candidate slots to be checked before doing full key comparisons. SIMD can compare multiple control bytes at once on supported CPUs, while the layout and growth strategy improve cache locality and lookup performance.

item.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Storage Version Migration Enabled by Default (3 minute read)
item.description: Storage version migration (SVM) is now generally available in Kubernetes v1.37, stable and enabled by default across all clusters running that version. The feature lets cluster administrators migrate stored API resources to a current storage version by creating a declarative StorageVersionMigration object, which the built-in control plane controller then handles automatically. Previously, admins had to rely on manual kubectl scripts or a separate out-of-tree component called kube-storage-version-migrator.

item.title: Wasmi 2.0 - Engineering of the Fastest Wasm Interpreters (23 minute read)

The release also preserves fast startup, adds options to reduce binary size, and includes stable fuel metering, deterministic WebAssembly support, and an improved CLI.

item.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Pod Certificates and Cluster Trust Bundles (3 minute read)
item.description: Kubernetes 1.37 brings Pod Certificates and Cluster Trust Bundles to general availability, adding X.509 certificate issuance for TLS and mTLS directly into core Kubernetes. The feature is designed as an alternative to service account JWTs, which are bearer tokens, meaning anyone who receives a copy of the token can use it to impersonate the workload. Pod Certificates use proof-of-possession credentials, so a workload proves it holds a private key without ever sending that key to a peer. The Kubernetes project has also released Tinycert, a third-party signer for experimenting with Pod Certificates, since no built-in signers ship with core Kubernetes yet.

item.title: Bug Blindness (12 minute read)

The tool includes five patch variants with increasing levels of security bypass, and exposes a control socket for screenshots, touch input, and clipboard access, which can be used for AI-driven end-to-end testing via a companion MCP server.

item.title: Scale before the spike: Predictive autoscaling for GPU workloads on Kubernetes (6 minute read)
item.description: Two Adobe platform engineers built a predictive Kubernetes autoscaler after a production incident left users seeing 15-20% error rates because reactive scaling fired too late to help. The system uses a Bi-LSTM model embedded in a Go controller binary to forecast demand 10 minutes ahead, running inference every 60 seconds against the past hour of Prometheus metrics. A graduated scaler caps scale-out at 20 pods per minute to avoid overwhelming the scheduler, and a burst detector adds a heuristic safety net for traffic spikes the model wasn't trained on. In hackathon validation, 23 out of 23 checks passed, with the predictor catching simulated spike patterns 11 minutes early.

item.title: Creepy crawlies (7 minute read)

item.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Garhwal (32 minute read)
item.description: Kubernetes v1.37, themed "Garhwal" after a Himalayan region of Uttarakhand, India, ships 67 enhancements: 16 promoted to Stable, 23 to Beta, 27 entering Alpha, and 1 deprecation or removal. Notable Stable graduations include the metrics.k8s.io API, which spent nearly nine years in Beta, and KYAML, a safer YAML subset for Kubernetes. The release also enables memory QoS and concurrent watch object decoding by default, and brings HorizontalPodAutoscaler scale-to-zero support to Beta. item.description: Archify is a Node.js tool for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI, and OpenCode that takes a codebase or system description and compiles it into an interactive HTML/SVG diagram. item.title: Tailcat (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Tailcat is a userspace networking tool that reuses Tailscale's WireGuard data plane without requiring the Tailscale control plane, account, root access, or routing-table changes. Two peers exchange a short connection token out of band, bootstrap through DERP, and then upgrade to a direct peer-to-peer UDP path when NAT traversal succeeds. It can also tunnel TCP ports, SSH, SOCKS5 traffic, and exit-node access.

item.title: Building an AI factory on Kubernetes (10 minute read)
item.description: Building an AI factory on Kubernetes means solving two problems at once: keeping GPU utilization high and keeping tenants from interfering with each other on the same hardware. The stack to do it now exists mostly from CNCF and open source projects, including DRA (GA in Kubernetes 1.34), HAMi for software-based GPU partitioning, vCluster for per-tenant virtual control planes, KServe for inference, and OpenCost for per-tenant chargeback. Network and storage isolation increasingly get pushed into hardware, with DPUs such as NVIDIA BlueField handling enforcement off the host CPU.

item.title: How we saved 100 terabytes of memory by optimizing 1.1.1.1's DNS cache (10 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare cut memory usage across its Big Pineapple DNS platform by roughly 100 terabytes after five successive changes to how cache entries are stored. The optimizations reduced the per-entry memory footprint from 953 bytes to 420 bytes, a 56% reduction across more than 250 billion cache entries. At p99, per-instance resident memory fell from 9.3 GB to 5.3 GB. Cache insert throughput also rose 43% and lookup latency dropped 19%, as the changes reduced allocations and improved memory locality.
